operations.specification: Accepts email and password in request body. Validates email format and password strength (min 8 chars). Checks if email already exists in todo_app_users. If exists, returns 409 Conflict. Hashes password using bcrypt before creating new todo_app_users record with current timestamp for created_at and updated_at. Returns JWT access token and refresh token in response with 201 Created.
operations.description:
The join operation allows a new user to register for the TodoApp service by providing a unique email and a secure password.

The operation references the todo_app_users table, specifically using the email and password_hash columns. The system verifies that the email does not already exist in the database to prevent duplicate accounts. Upon successful validation, the password is cryptographically hashed using bcrypt and stored in the password_hash column. The user record is created with the current timestamp in created_at and updated_at fields, ensuring immutable audit trails.

Security is paramount: passwords are never stored in plain text. Validation ensures the password meets minimum complexity requirements (minimum 8 characters). Email format is validated using standard RFC 5322 rules to prevent malformed inputs. This ensures data integrity at the point of entry.

The operation signals success with a 201 Created HTTP status and returns an access token and refresh token in the response body using the ITodoAppUser.IAuthorized type, enabling immediate authentication. The tokens are signed and time-limited. This operation is the first step in establishing a fully authenticated user session.

Related operations include login (which shares the same credentials validation logic) and refresh (which extends session validity). Unlike login, join creates a new user account; unlike refresh, it does not renew existing credentials.

requestBody.description: Contains email and password needed to create a new user account.

responseBody.description: Contains the access token and refresh token issued upon successful registration.

operations.name: join

operations.specification: Accepts email and password in request body. Looks up user in todo_app_users by email. Compares provided password with stored password_hash using bcrypt compare. If no user found or password mismatch, returns 401 Unauthorized. If valid, generates JWT access token and refresh token, stores refresh token in user_session (via external system), and returns them in response with 200 OK.
operations.description:
The login operation authenticates an existing user by validating their email and password against the todo_app_users table. It references the email and password_hash columns to locate the user and verify credentials using bcrypt password comparison.

The system returns a 401 Unauthorized response if either the email does not exist in the database or if the provided password does not match the stored hash. This prevents information leakage about account existence. Upon successful authentication, a cryptographically signed JWT access token is generated with an expiration, and a refresh token is issued and stored securely in the user_session table (managed externally by system).

The response body returns these two tokens using the ITodoAppUser.IAuthorized type, allowing the client to use the access token for subsequent authenticated API calls. Refresh tokens enable session renewal without requiring the user to re-enter credentials. The operation is stateless from the server's perspective—only the refresh token in the session store maintains persistent session state.

This operation is the core of user authentication. It must be called prior to any protected endpoint. It is not required for switching between roles, as there is only one actor type, and cannot be chained as a prerequisite to other operations since authentication is enforced at endpoint level via authorizationActor, not via prerequisite dependencies.

requestBody.description: Contains email and password for credential validation.

responseBody.description: Contains the access token and refresh token issued upon successful login.

operations.name: login

operations.specification: Accepts refresh_token in request body. Validates refresh token against user_session table. If valid and not expired, regenerates JWT access token with new expiration and issue time, optionally generates new refresh token (if rotation policy enabled), updates user_session expiration, and returns new tokens in response with 200 OK. Returns 401 if refresh token is invalid or expired.
operations.description:
The refresh operation renews an expired access token by validating a previously issued refresh token against stored session records in the user_session entity (managed externally). This token is not stored in the todo_app_users table, but rather maintained in a system-managed session store.

The operation ensures security by enforcing refresh token validity and expiration checks. If the refresh token is invalid, revoked, or expired, the system returns a 401 Unauthorized status, forcing the user to re-authenticate via login. On success, a new access token is generated with a fresh expiration, meeting JWT stateless requirements.

The refresh token may or may not be rotated (replaced) based on system policy, but in either case, the session's expiration is extended. The operation returns updated tokens using the ITodoAppUser.IAuthorized type to ensure the client maintains authenticated access.

This operation is called when the access token expires. It is not a prerequisite for any other operation and does not alter user state beyond extending the authentication window. Users without an active session cannot invoke this endpoint. This operation is essential for maintaining seamless user experiences without frequent relogins.

requestBody.description: Contains a valid refresh token to renew access credentials.

responseBody.description: Contains new access token and optionally new refresh token upon successful renewal.

operations.name: refresh

operations.description:
Retrieve the authenticated user's private profile information including display name, account creation date, and last update timestamp.

This operation returns exactly one resource: the profile entity associated with the authenticated user whose JWT token is provided in the request header. The response contains no information about any other user, and attempting to access another user's profile will result in HTTP 404 Not Found.

Profile data is completely private and isolated. Even when viewing a list of todos, no profile information (display name, email, or user ID) from any other user is ever included in responses. The system enforces data isolation at the database query layer — every query includes a WHERE clause matching the authenticated user ID, ensuring no SQL injection or data leakage can occur.

No other API endpoint returns profile data. When a user edits their profile, the old value is preserved in audit logs, but those logs are never exposed through the API. Recovery of delete accounts from backups is handled at the infrastructure level and never accessible via API endpoints.

Related operation: PUT /todo_app_profiles updates the display name; this operation is the read counterpart.
operations.name: at
operations.specification: Query todo_app_profiles table by userId matching the authenticated user ID extracted from JWT token. Return only displayName, createdAt, and updatedAt fields. Ensure no joins or subqueries include any data from other tables or users. Use secondary index on userId for performance. If user ID is not found in profiles table, return 404 (should never occur if user has valid JWT and registered).

operations.description:
Update the authenticated user's display name.

This operation allows a user to change their visible name within the application. The display name is the only user-editable attribute in the profile. All other profile data—including user ID, account creation timestamp, and last update timestamp—are immutable system-managed fields that are never editable via API.

The display name must satisfy strict validation rules: between 1 and 100 characters, excluding HTML tags, special control characters, and leading/trailing whitespace. The system does not allow display names that contain forbidden characters: <, >, &, ", ', \, /, *, ?, |, :, 

Access to this endpoint is restricted exclusively to the authenticated user. Any attempt to update a profile belonging to another user results in HTTP 403 Forbidden with error code PROFILE_ACCESS_DENIED.

This operation does not affect any todo data, history, or trash entries. Profile updates are purely cosmetic and do not trigger audit logs beyond the updatedAt timestamp update.
operations.name: update
operations.specification: Extract display name from request body. Validate against length (1–100 chars) and character set restrictions (no forbidden characters). Look up authenticated user via JWT token. Update the todo_app_profiles table SET displayName = ?, updatedAt = NOW() WHERE userId = ? (verified from JWT). If update fails due to constraint violation, throw 400 with error PROFILE_DISPLAY_NAME_INVALID. Return updated profile with: userId, displayName, createdAt, updatedAt. Do not return email, password, or session tokens.

responseBody.description: Updated profile information including internal immutable fields

requestBody.description: Contains the new display name for the authenticated user's profile

operations.description:
Retrieve a specific todo item by its unique identifier.

This endpoint returns complete details of a single todo item owned by the authenticated user. The system validates that the todo exists and belongs to the calling user using the JWT-embedded user ID. If the todo is soft-deleted (has a non-null deleted_at), the system returns HTTP 404 Not Found to prevent disclosure of deleted data.

The response includes all fields: title, description, start_date, due_date, is_completed, created_at, updated_at, and deleted_at to preserve full context. This view is used by the todo detail screen in the frontend application.

This operation depends on successful JWT authentication. Unauthorized clients receive HTTP 401. Access to todos not owned by the user returns HTTP 404 for security isolation.

Related operations:
- GET /todos for list view with pagination and filters
- PATCH /todos/{todoId}/toggle-status to change completion state
- DELETE /todos/{todoId} to soft-delete the todo
- GET /todos/{todoId}/history to view edit history
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query todo_app_todos table with WHERE clause on id = {todoId} AND todo_app_user_id = {userIdFromJWT} AND deleted_at IS NULL.
Return full record if found.
If todo not found or belongs to other user, return HTTP 404 Not Found.
If todo exists but has non-null deleted_at, return HTTP 404 Not Found to mask soft-deleted records.
Use single database query with join to validate user ownership.
Do not use caching - todo data is personal and frequently updated.

responseBody.description: Full detail of the requested todo item

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the todo item to retrieve. Must be a valid UUID.
parameters.name: todoId

operations.specification: Query todo_app_todos table with pagination, filtering by completion status, and sorting by createdAt, startDate, or dueDate. Filter by userId from JWT token. Support filtering by status parameter (all/completed/incomplete). Sort ascending or descending by specified field. Limit results by perPage parameter (default 10). Use cursor-based or offset-based pagination. Include only todos not marked as deleted. Return total count for pagination controls.
operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered, sorted, and paginated list of todo items belonging to the authenticated user.

This operation supports comprehensive filtering by completion status (all, completed, incomplete), pagination with configurable page size, and sorting by creation date, start date, or due date. The response contains summary information optimized for display in todo list interfaces.

Only todos owned by the authenticated user (validated via JWT) are returned. Non-existent or inaccessible todos result in HTTP 404. Soft-deleted todos are excluded from results. This endpoint is the primary way users view their todo list and must support efficient querying for large datasets.

Related operations: GET /todos/{id} for detailed view, PATCH /todos/{id}/toggle-status for status toggling, and DELETE /todos/{id} for soft deletion.

requestBody.description: Filter, sort, and pagination parameters for the todo list

operations.name: index

operations.specification: Create a new todo item with required title and optional description, startDate, and dueDate. Assign ownership to authenticated user. Set completed field to false by default. Preserve createdAt timestamp at creation time. Validate required fields before insert. Return 201 Created with empty body. Reject any attempt to set completed, deleted, or id fields via request body.
operations.description:
Create a new todo item for the authenticated user.

This endpoint allows users to create a new task with a required title and optional description, start date, and due date. The todo is automatically assigned to the authenticated user and created with a default completion status of false (incomplete).

All creation operations are atomic and subject to validation: the title field must be non-empty and within supported length limits. Description, startDate, and dueDate are optional and will be stored as null if not provided. The system enforces that users may not set or override the completed, deleted, createdAt, or id fields during creation; these values are managed internally.

This operation respects ownership boundaries: a user cannot create a todo on behalf of another user. The operation requires valid JWT authentication and validates user context before persistence.

requestBody.description: Details for creating a new todo item.

operations.name: create

operations.description:
Update an existing todo's editable attributes: title, description, start_date, and due_date. This operation is available only to the authenticated user who owns the todo. The completion status (is_completed) cannot be changed via this endpoint; use PATCH /todos/{todoId}/toggle-status for that purpose.

The todo must not be soft-deleted (deleted_at must be null). If the todo does not exist, belongs to another user, or is already deleted, returns HTTP 404 Not Found with error code TODO_NOT_FOUND.

All date fields (start_date, due_date) must be provided in ISO 8601 format. If omitted, the existing value is preserved. Title is required and must not be empty. Description can be null or empty string. The updated_at timestamp is automatically set to the current time. A new edit history record is created for every successful update.

This operation does not modify the todo's creation timestamp or deleted_at status. The ACID properties of the update are guaranteed, and a concurrent edit by another operation will result in an optimistic lock failure.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Query todo_app_todos by id and todo_app_user_id to verify ownership and active status (deleted_at IS NULL). Validate request body fields: title is required and non-empty, start_date and due_date are valid ISO 8601 timestamps if provided.

Perform atomic update within a transaction: update the todo's title, description, start_date, due_date, and set updated_at to current timestamp. Ensure no changes are made to is_completed or deleted_at.

If update is successful, insert a new record into todo_app_todo_histories with the old values, current user_id, and timestamp. Return the full updated todo entity. If the todo is not found or already deleted, return 404. If concurrent update detected (optimistic lock), return 409 Conflict.

responseBody.description: The updated todo entity with all fields including updated timestamps.

parameters.description: Unique identifier for the todo entity to be updated. Must belong to the authenticated user.
parameters.name: todoId

requestBody.description: The fields that can be edited: title, description, start_date, and due_date. Title is required; others are optional. Omitted fields retain their current value.

operations.description:
Permanently delete a todo item and its entire edit history from the database.

This operation irreversibly removes the todo from the system. All data — including title, description, start date, due date, completion status, and creation timestamp — is completely purged.

All associated edit history records are also permanently deleted in a cascading operation, as specified in trash management requirements.

This action cannot be undone. The todo will no longer appear in any list, including the trash.

The system ensures strict privacy: only the authenticated user can delete their own todos. Attempting to delete another user’s todo returns 404 (not 403) to prevent enumeration.

For restoration or partial deletion, other endpoints exist — this operation is final and complete.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
Perform soft-delete on a todo item by setting todo_app_todos.deletedAt to the current timestamp. Only process if todo.appUserId matches authenticatedUserId (enforced by service layer). Use database transaction to ensure atomicity.

No changes to todo_app_todo_histories — this is explicitly preserved per requirements.

Return HTTP 204 No Content upon success.

If todo.appUserId does not match authenticatedUserId → return HTTP 404 (not 403), to prevent enumeration attacks.

If todo does not exist → return HTTP 404.

All queries must include WHERE todo_app_todos.appUserId = $authUserId to enforce privacy.

No caching of deleted todos in any client-side layer — the system ensures immediate removal from visible lists.

No logging of specific todo content; only log operation type, userId, and timestamp for audit — never expose todo text or metadata to logs.

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the todo item to delete. Must belong to the authenticated user.
parameters.name: todoId

operations.specification: Query todo_app_todos table where deleted_at is not null and todo_app_user_id = authenticatedUserId. Support filtering by deletion time range (deleted_atgte, deleted_atlte). Support sorting by created_at or deleted_at in ascending/descending order. Return cursor-based pagination with page and perPage parameters. Exclude any todos with deleted_at = null. Do not join with todo_app_todo_histories unless requested via expanded flag (not required per spec).
operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of todos that have been soft-deleted by the authenticated user.

This operation provides access to the user's personal trash, containing all todos marked for deletion but not yet permanently purged. Users can filter by the timestamp range when the todo was deleted and sort the results by either the original creation timestamp or the deletion timestamp.

The response includes only minimal summary information (title, completion status, creation date, deletion date) to optimize for list display performance. Full details and edit history can be retrieved via individual todo restoration or history endpoints.

All data returned is exclusively owned by the authenticated user. No other user’s deleted todos are visible or accessible. System-enforced ownership validation ensures data isolation at the database query level.

This endpoint is intended for users reviewing, restoring, or permanently deleting items from their trash. The operation requires no request parameters by default but supports complex search criteria through the request body for advanced filtering.

requestBody.description: Search and filter criteria for trash items.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of deleted todo summaries.

operations.name: index

operations.description:
Record a new edit history entry when a todo's title, description, startDate, or dueDate is modified.

When a user edits any of the allowed fields on a todo, the system creates a dedicated history entry documenting the before and after values. This ensures full auditability of intentional changes to todo metadata while preserving the immutability of the todo's completion status and creation timestamp.

The operation is designed with strict validation: only title, description, startDate, and dueDate fields may be submitted. Attempts to modify other fields (like completion status or ID) will result in an error. The edit history is automatically linked to the authenticated user and the specific todo item.

This history is separate from toggle event logging. Toggle events (changing completion status) are recorded in a different audit trail and do not appear in this history.

The returned response includes the full history entry with its timestamp, providing immediate feedback about the successful edit recording. This enables clients to update their local state or display the new history entry without needing a separate request.
operations.name: create
operations.specification: Validate that requested todo exists and belongs to authenticated user. Verify that request body contains only allowed editable fields: title, description, startDate, dueDate. For each field provided, compare current database value to proposed value. If any value has changed, record old value as before_* and new value as after_* in a new todo_app_todo_histories record. Include current timestamp as edited_at. Do NOT record empty changes. Return created history record with ID and timestamps. Handle any database constraint violations or integrity failures with appropriate error responses.

responseBody.description: The created edit history record with before/after values and timestamp.

parameters.description: The unique identifier of the todo to edit.
parameters.name: todoId

requestBody.description: Fields to edit on the todo, with new values. Only title, description, startDate, and dueDate are permitted.

operations.description:
Retrieve the complete edit history for a specific todo item.

This endpoint returns a chronological log of all field-level changes made to the todo, including the before and after values of any modified fields (title, description, start date, due date). History entries are ordered from most recent to oldest by timestamp.

Only the owner of the todo can access its edit history. Attempts to access history for a todo belonging to another user will return HTTP 404 Not Found. If no edits have been made, an empty array will be returned.

The history data is persisted independently from the todo itself and is automatically removed when the todo is permanently deleted.
operations.name: at
operations.specification: Query the todo_app_todo_histories table for all records where todo_app_todo_id = {id} AND the associated todo owner matches the authenticated user ID. Sort results by edited_at in descending order. Return array of history records with fields: id, todo_app_todo_id, edited_at, before_title, after_title, before_description, after_description, before_startdate, after_startdate, before_duedate, after_duedate. If no records exist, return empty array. Apply ownership verification by joining with todo_app_todos table and comparing userID from JWT.

responseBody.description: Array of edit history records for the todo

ITodoAppTodo.description: Full detail response of a single todo item. Contains the complete state of a user-owned task including title, optional description and dates, completion status, timestamps for creation and last update, and soft-delete status. User identity is obfuscated to maintain privacy — instead of exposing the user ID, a lightweight summary of the actor is provided via reference. This schema is returned by GET /todoApp/user/todos/{todoId} operations.
ITodoAppTodo.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from todo_app_todos table. Excludes todo_app_user_id per security rules; actor identity resolved via JWT and exposed as $ref to ITodoAppUser.ISummary. All date fields use ISO 8601 format. Required fields: id, title, is_completed, created_at, updated_at. Nullable fields (description, start_date, due_date, deleted_at) use oneOf with null. No computed fields. Aggregation relation 'histories' is handled by separate endpoint GET /todos/{id}/history.

ITodoAppTodo.ISummary.description: Lightweight representation of a todo item for display in paginated lists, such as the main todo list and the trash. Contains only essential information needed to render a list item: title, completion status, creation time, and optional start/due dates. Does not include the detailed description or any edit history. Used in response bodies of GET /todos and GET /trash endpoints. Fields with null values indicate absence of data, per user's input.

ITodoAppTodoHistory.description: Immutable audit record capturing every edit to a todo's metadata. Records the exact state before and after each change to title, description, start date, or due date, along with the precise timestamp of the edit. Used for compliance, accountability, and full change history tracking. Contains no user identifiers or system flags — only the changed data values and timing.
ITodoAppTodoHistory.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from todo_app_todo_histories model. Represents immutable audit log of all field-level changes made to a todo item. Each history entry records before/after values for title, description, start_date, and due_date along with exact timestamp. Used exclusively for compliance and change tracking. Not subject to modification or truncation. All data is sourced directly from the database and never computed.

refresh_token.description: A refresh token string used to obtain a new access token when the current one expires. This token is securely stored server-side in the session table and is never transmitted in plain form during regular API calls — only during the refresh endpoint invocation.
refresh_token.x-autobe-specification: The refresh_token is an opaque, client-provided string presented during token refresh requests. This string is not a column in the database but represents a token issued by the authentication system and stored server-side in the todo_app_user_sessions table's internal token storage. The server validates this string against its session store; if valid and unexpired, it issues new tokens. This DTO accepts only this string input. The column 'token' does not exist in the todo_app_user_sessions schema - the actual token storage mechanism is internal to the session management layer and not exposed as a column.

ITodoAppTodo.IRequest.description: Request parameters for filtering, sorting, and paginating todo item lists. Used by both the main todo list and trash endpoints to control the subset and order of returned items.
ITodoAppTodo.IRequest.x-autobe-specification: Query parameter schema for filtering, sorting, and paginating todo lists. Used exclusively for GET /todoApp/user/todos and GET /todoApp/user/trash endpoints. All values are extracted from request query parameters, not mapped from database columns. Backend applies user context from JWT to scope all queries. Defaults: status=all, sortBy=createdAt, sortDirection=desc, page=1, perPage=10. limit defaults to 100 if not provided. All parameters are validated against type and enum constraints, then normalized before database query execution.

ITodoAppUser.ISummary.description: Lightweight summary of the authenticated user for display purposes. Contains only the user's display name and account metadata (creation and last update timestamps). Does not include email, internal ID, authentication status, or sensitive information. Used in API responses to represent user ownership without revealing private details.
ITodoAppUser.ISummary.x-autobe-specification: The display_name is pulled from todo_app_profiles.display_name. The created_at and updated_at are pulled from todo_app_profiles.created_at and updated_at. No other fields are accessible. This schema is designed to expose only what is necessary for UI display while maintaining strict privacy isolation. The data originates from todo_app_profiles, not todo_app_users, to separate identity from authentication.
